# Live View & Video Autofocus

Contrast-detect and hybrid AF in live view and movie modes: Face+Tracking, FlexiZone Multi/Single, Quick mode, Movie Servo AF, touch shutter, and AF behavior differences from viewfinder shooting

Live View and video autofocus on the Canon EOS Rebel T5i / 700D uses contrast-detect AF (image sensor) for most methods, with the exception of Quick mode which uses the dedicated phase-detection AF sensor — the same sensor used in viewfinder shooting.

## AF Methods in Live View

Four AF methods are available in Live View still shooting. Select via the [A] tab → [AF method], or the Quick Control (Q button) [1]:

- **u (Face)+Tracking** — detects human faces; the AF point (⟨p⟩) moves to track a detected face. If multiple faces are present, press the directional key to choose the target. If no face is detected, or if you tap the screen without selecting a face, the camera falls back to FlexiZone-Multi with automatic selection [1].
- **FlexiZone-Multi** — up to 31 AF points (automatic selection) covering a wide area, or divided into 9 zones (zone selection, Creative Zone modes only; Basic Zone modes use automatic selection only). During still shooting with Continuous AF or Movie Servo AF enabled, if no subject is detected the AF point briefly appears at center; pressing the shutter halfway focuses in FlexiZone-Multi automatic mode [1].
- **FlexiZone-Single** — single AF point; use the directional keys (or tap the LCD) to position it. Supports magnified view (5× or 10×) for precise focus confirmation; AF speed may differ between normal and magnified views [1].
- **Quick mode** — uses the dedicated AF sensor (phase-detect) via One-Shot AF, identical to viewfinder AF behavior. Fastest focus acquisition, but the Live View image is interrupted momentarily while the mirror flips down for AF. Cannot be used for movie shooting. Setting Quick mode automatically disables Continuous AF [1].

**Lens note:** For lenses EF50mm f/1.4 USM, EF50mm f/1.8 II, EF50mm f/2.5 Compact Macro, EF75-300mm f/4-5.6 III, and EF75-300mm f/4-5.6 III USM, Quick mode is recommended — the contrast-detect methods (u+Tracking, FlexiZone-Multi, FlexiZone-Single) may focus slowly or fail with these lenses [1].

## Continuous AF (Live View Still Shooting)

Default setting: **Enable**. Keeps focus near the subject continuously so pressing the shutter button results in faster final AF. Trade-off: the lens operates frequently, consuming more battery and reducing shot count. Setting AF method to Quick mode automatically forces Continuous AF to Disable; switching back to another method restores the original Continuous AF setting [1].

Always turn off power before switching the lens focus mode switch to MF when Continuous AF is enabled [1].

## Touch Shutter

Tap the LCD monitor to focus and take the picture automatically; works in all shooting modes [1]. Enable/disable by tapping the [y]/[x] icon at the bottom left of the screen, or via [A] tab → [Touch Shutter: Enable] [1].

- When tapping with **FlexiZone-Multi** set, the camera switches to FlexiZone-Single at the tapped point.
- Continuous shooting mode reverts to single shooting via Touch Shutter.
- Touch Shutter does not work in magnified view.
- For bulb exposure: first tap starts exposure, second tap ends it.
- Touch Shutter has no effect when Custom Function [6: Shutter/AE lock button] is set to [1: AE lock/AF] or [3: AE/AF, no AE lock] [1].

## Movie Servo AF

Available in movie mode; default setting: **Enable** [2].

- **Enable**: Camera continuously focuses on moving subjects during recording. The EF-S18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS STM and EF-S18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS STM lenses minimize focusing noise in the recording; other lenses may record audible mechanical sound (use the Directional Stereo Microphone DM-E1 to reduce this) [2].
- **Disable**: Focus only when the shutter button is pressed halfway; no continuous tracking [2].

**Pausing Movie Servo AF** (to hold focus or avoid noise):
- Tap the [⬛] icon on the lower left of the screen.
- Press the AF-OFF button.
- Hold the AE lock button (if C.Fn [6: Shutter/AE lock button] = [2: AF/AF lock, no AE lock]).
When paused, the AF point turns gray. Performing the same operation resumes Movie Servo AF. Navigating to the menu and returning also resumes it [2].

**Movie Servo AF cautions** [2]:
- Consumes additional battery power, reducing possible shots and recording time.
- Movie Servo AF stops momentarily during zoom or image magnification.
- If a subject moves toward/away from the camera or the camera pans, the recorded image may momentarily expand or contract (change in magnification).
- Fast-moving subjects approaching or receding, or subjects at close distance in front of the camera, are difficult to focus.

## AF with Shutter Button During Movie Recording

Setting: **[Z2] → [AF with shutter button during movie recording]** [2].

- **ONE SHOT** (default): pressing shutter halfway refocuses before taking a still; reliable for static subjects.
- **Disable**: shutter immediately captures without seeking focus; useful when timing matters more than sharp focus [2].

## AF Method in Movie Mode

Movie mode supports three AF methods: **u+Tracking**, **FlexiZone-Multi**, and **FlexiZone-Single**. Quick mode is not available for movie shooting [1][2].

In movie shooting with FlexiZone-Single selected, the AF point is displayed at a larger size when Movie Servo AF is enabled [1]. For movies, the available AF point count changes by resolution: 21 AF points (3 zones) at 1920×1080 and 1280×720; 25 AF points (9 zones) at 640×480 [1].

## AF Behavior Differences: Live View vs. Viewfinder

- Live View contrast-detect AF (u+Tracking, FlexiZone-Multi, FlexiZone-Single) is slower than viewfinder phase-detect AF; pressing the shutter button halfway focuses again even if focus was already achieved [1].
- No AF-assist beam is emitted in Live View (contrast-detect methods); an EX-series Speedlite with LED will turn on its LED light for assist when needed [1].
- In Live View, image brightness may change during and after AF operation [1].
- When pressing the shutter halfway during movie recording, side-effects include: momentary loss of focus, momentary brightness change, brief freeze of the recorded image, and possible audible lens noise [2].

## Conditions That Make Live View AF Difficult

Low-contrast subjects (blue sky, solid-color surfaces, blown highlights/shadows), low light, horizontal-only contrast patterns, repetitive patterns, fine lines, changing light sources, night scenes, very small subjects, edge-of-frame subjects, strongly reflective subjects, mixed near/far subjects in one AF point, moving subjects, subject far out of focus initially, soft-focus or special-effect lenses, and image noise [1].

# Lens AF Motors & Manual Focus

Lens-side AF motor types (STM, USM, micro-motor), AF/MF switching, full-time manual focus, and how lens AF type affects body AF performance in viewfinder, live view, and video

The two Canon EF-S 18-55mm kit lenses illustrate the practical difference between lens AF motor types and how those types shape focus behaviour across shooting modes.

## Motor types compared

**EF-S18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS II** uses a conventional (micro-motor) drive. AF is mechanical; the focusing ring rotates physically during autofocus. The manual warns: do not touch the rotating parts of the lens while autofocus is active, and do not adjust focus manually when the focus mode switch is set to AF [1].

**EF-S18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS STM** uses a stepping motor with lead screws. The motor drives the focus lens electronically and also controls focus lens position during zooming [2]. This architecture enables:
- Quiet, smooth **Movie Servo AF** (continuous AF during video) [2]
- High-speed, quiet autofocusing during viewfinder shooting [2]
- **Electronic manual focus** — the focusing ring has no direct mechanical link; rotation is detected electronically [2]
- **Full-time manual focus (FTM)**: after the subject locks in ONE SHOT AF, pressing the shutter halfway and turning the focusing ring fine-tunes focus without switching modes [2]

## AF/MF switching

Both lenses have a physical **focus mode switch** (AF / MF positions).

**IS II**: Setting the switch to MF disables autofocus entirely. Turn the focusing ring to focus. No manual adjustment is possible while the switch is in AF [1].

**IS STM**: Same switch positions, but adds full-time MF capability — after AF acquisition in ONE SHOT AF mode, you can override by pressing the shutter halfway and turning the focusing ring [2]. Quickly rotating the focusing ring may result in delayed focus due to the electronic drive [2].

## STM-specific power and sleep behaviour

Because the STM's motor controls focus mechanically through electronics, several power states affect it:

- **Camera OFF**: the motor does not operate. Manual focus adjustments are not possible. Zooming causes delayed focus [2].
- **Sleep mode**: if the lens is not operated for a set period, it enters sleep mode even with the camera ON. MF is not possible, zooming causes delayed focus. Press the shutter halfway to exit sleep mode [2].
- **Initial reset**: when the camera powers on (or wakes from auto power off), the lens performs an initial focus reset — the viewfinder image goes out of focus briefly. Wait approximately 1 second after reset completes before shooting [2].

These states do not apply to the IS II's mechanical motor.

## Movie Servo AF compatibility (STM)

Movie Servo AF is compatible only with specific bodies. As of June 2013: EOS REBEL T5i/700D, EOS REBEL SL1/100D, EOS REBEL T4i/650D, and EOS M (with Mount Adapter EF-EOS M) [2]. Other EF-S–compatible bodies can mount the STM lens but will not use Movie Servo AF.

## Extenders

Neither lens supports EF extenders. The IS II explicitly states the EF1.4X III and EF2X III cannot be used [1]; the IS STM states extenders cannot be used [2].

## Focus mode and close-up accessories

When using Extension Tubes (EF12 II or EF25 II) or Close-up lenses with either lens, manual focus (MF mode) is recommended for accurate focusing [1][2]. The STM version notes that MF mode is recommended for close-up lens use as well [2].

# AF Operation Modes & Point Selection

T5i/700D viewfinder AF: One-Shot (still subjects, focus lock), AI Servo (continuous tracking), AI Focus (auto-switch); manual vs. auto 9-point selection; cross-type sensitivity by aperture; AF-assist beam; difficult subjects; MF fallback.

The T5i/700D viewfinder uses phase-detection AF with 9 AF points. To enable autofocus, the lens focus mode switch must be set to **AF**. In Basic Zone modes, AF operation is set automatically; in Creative Zone modes (P, Tv, Av, M) you select it manually [1].

## AF Operation Modes

### One-Shot AF (still subjects)
Press the shutter button halfway — the camera focuses once and locks. The AF point that achieved focus lights up briefly in red, and the focus confirmation light **◉** in the viewfinder lights up. With evaluative metering, exposure is set at the same moment focus is achieved. Focus stays locked as long as you hold the shutter button halfway, letting you recompose. If focus cannot be achieved, **◉** blinks and the shutter is disabled; see Subjects Difficult to Focus below [1].

### AI Servo AF (moving subjects)
The camera focuses continuously while the shutter button is held halfway. Exposure is set at the moment of capture, not at focus lock. With automatic AF point selection, the camera starts on the center AF point and continues tracking if the subject moves to another AF point. The beeper does not sound and **◉** does not light up when focus is achieved [1].

### AI Focus AF (auto-switching)
Starts in One-Shot AF; automatically switches to AI Servo AF if the subject begins moving. When Servo operation is active, the beeper sounds softly and continuously, but **◉** does not light up and focus is not locked [1].

## AF Point Selection

**Automatic selection** (Basic Zone modes default): all 9 AF points light up; the camera focuses the closest subject automatically.

**Manual selection** (Creative Zone modes): press the **◻** button, then use the directional keys or turn the Main Dial to highlight the desired AF point in red in the viewfinder. Pressing **SET** toggles between the center point and full automatic selection. During manual selection you can also tap the touchscreen to pick a point; tapping the icon at the bottom left switches back to automatic selection [1].

**Tip for portraits:** use One-Shot AF, manually select the center AF point, focus on the subject's eye, then recompose. For moving subjects use automatic selection + AI Servo AF [1].

## Cross-Type Sensitivity by Aperture

| Max. aperture | Center AF point | Off-center AF points (8 points) |
|---|---|---|
| f/5.6 or faster | Cross-type (H + V) | Cross-type (H + V)* |
| f/2.8 or faster | High-precision cross-type (H + V) | Cross-type (H + V) |

*Some older lenses (e.g. EF35-80mm f/4-5.6, EF80-200mm f/4.5-5.6 USM series) restrict the six side AF points to horizontal-only detection and the top/bottom points to vertical-only — cross-type works only on the center point with these lenses.

If using an Extender causes the maximum aperture to drop below f/5.6, viewfinder AF is disabled entirely (Live View AF methods still work in that case) [1].

## AF-Assist Beam

Under low light, pressing the shutter button halfway causes the built-in flash to fire brief bursts to illuminate the subject for AF. Effective range: approx. **4 m / 13.1 ft**. The beam is not emitted in Landscape (▲), Sports (⑤), or No-Flash (□) modes, nor during AI Servo AF. In Creative Zone modes, the flash must be raised with the flash button; Custom Function **C.Fn-4: AF-assist beam firing** can disable the beam entirely [1].

## Subjects Difficult to Focus

AF may fail (**◉** blinks) with:
- Very low-contrast subjects (blue sky, solid-color walls)
- Very low light
- Extremely backlit or highly reflective subjects (e.g. car body)
- AF point covering both a near and a far subject (e.g. animal in a cage)
- Repetitive patterns (skyscraper windows, keyboard)

**Workarounds:**
1. With One-Shot AF: focus on an object at the same distance as the subject, lock focus, then recompose.
2. Set the lens focus mode switch to **MF** and turn the focusing ring until the subject is sharp in the viewfinder.

During manual focusing, half-pressing the shutter button still activates the AF point indicator (lights red) and **◉** if the focused area is sharp [1].

For Live View difficult-subject guidance, see `live_view_autofocus`.

# Sigma MC-11 AF Compatibility

Sigma MC-11 (SA-to-E) AF support: Sony E-mount body list (α1–ZV-E1, June 2025) and per-lens AFS/AFC/AFA/DMF table for 30 Art, Contemporary, and Sports lenses. AFC/AFA unsupported; teleconverters incompatible; DMF needs USB Dock on select lenses; MF required for video.

Sigma MC-11 (SA-to-E mount converter) general operation has been verified against all listed Sony E-mount bodies as of June 2025 [1]. Compatibility is confirmed but not guaranteed for all functions and performance.

## Compatible camera bodies

All AF checks conducted by Sigma as of June 2025 [1]:

α1II, α1, α9II, α9, α7RV, α7RIV, α7RIII, α7RII, α7R, α7SIII, α7SII, α7S, α7CR, α7CII, α7C, α7IV, α7III, α7II, α7, α6700, α6600, α6500, α6400, α6300, α6100, α6000, α5100, α5000, ZV-E10, ZV-E1.

## Global restrictions

- **AF-C is not supported** on any body [1].
- **Teleconverters cannot be used** with MC-11 [1].
- Only compatible Sigma SA-mount lenses are supported; other lenses are not guaranteed [1].
- **Use MF when shooting movies** [2].

## Per-lens AF compatibility

AFC and AFA are unsupported for all lenses. AFS is supported for all listed lenses. DMF availability varies by lens and requires changing settings via the USB Dock (sold separately) [2].
